fullPassage:
A Korean Chief in Nigeria

There is a Korean man who became the chief of a Nigerian tribe for making huge contributions to Nigeria's agriculture and economy. Here is his story.

Dr. Hahn is an agriculturist who specialized in plant breeding. Growing up right after the Korean war, he knew what it was like to be hungry, and he wanted to help people in need. In 1971, he was given two opportunities: work for Cambridge University or for the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture in Nigeria. On his way to Cambridge for a job interview, he first stopped in Nigeria. There, he saw the country had been destroyed by a civil war. More than 2 million people had died, and more than half a million people were starving. Dr. Hahn wanted to rescue Nigerians from hunger. So, he persuaded his family and moved to Nigeria.

When Dr. Hahn got there, he learned that the staple food in Nigeria was a plant called cassava. Unfortunately, cassava was defenseless against viral and bacterial diseases, so it did not yield much crop. Knowing this, he decided to develop stronger cassava varieties with higher yields. However, Dr. Hahn faced a problem: there was not much information available about cassava. Cassava was rarely studied or developed because it was not a cash crop. To make matters worse, he had never seen or eaten cassava before.

While studying African cassava, Dr. Hahn found out that the Europeans who colonized Brazil had first brought cassava into Africa. He immediately flew to Brazil to study the original cassava. There, he learned about it and went back to Nigeria with Brazilian cassava seeds. Then, Dr. Hahn traveled to every corner of Nigeria and collected different types of local cassava to see if they were good at fighting diseases, but they weren't. Fortunately, he found a plant that was similar to cassava but resistant to diseases. He started crossing this plant with the Brazilian cassava. After five years of hard work, Dr. Hahn finally succeeded in developing new varieties of cassava. They yielded much more than the local ones and could survive diseases.

Another obstacle Dr. Hahn faced was distributing the new varieties. Local farmers would not listen to a foreigner. To overcome this problem, Dr. Hahn visited markets, churches, and schools and gave out the new varieties to Nigerian people for free. He went from one house to the next to let farmers know the superiority of these new varieties. Sometimes he planted them in the middle of the cassava field without telling the farmers. His colleagues were concerned that the farmers might be angry to find different cassava in their fields. However, Dr. Hahn insisted that the farmers would think that it was a gift from God. He was right. The farmers soon realized the superiority of the new varieties, and more and more farmers started to cultivate them. Thanks to the new cassava, fewer people were starving. In fact, they could even make more money by selling the remaining cassava. Eventually, Nigeria became the country that produced the greatest amount of cassava in the world. In 1983, the Yoruba, a major tribe of Nigeria, honored Dr. Hahn as a chief with the title "Seriki Agbe" or "the King of Farmers."

In addition to cassava, Dr. Hahn developed other major foods, including yam, sweet potato, and banana. Soon, other African countries asked for his help. Dr. Hahn traveled to these countries to teach local farmers and scholars how to grow these new varieties. He spent 23 years developing and distributing the new cassava varieties to the whole continent. Although he left Nigeria in 1994, he is still remembered as one of the greatest scientists who fought against starvation in Africa. Dr. Hahn once said, "If you have faith that what you do will benefit humanity, I believe that you must sacrifice yourself. Even if I were to go back to the past, I would still do the same thing."

questions.passage: Dr. Hahn is an agriculturist who specialized in plant breeding. Growing up right after the Korean war, he knew what it was like to be hungry, and he wanted to help people in need. In 1971, he was given two opportunities: work for Cambridge University or for the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture in Nigeria. On his way to Cambridge for a job interview, he first stopped in Nigeria. There, he saw the country had been (A)[destroyed / constructed] by a civil war. More than 2 million people had died, and more than half a million people were (B)[starving / thriving]. Dr. Hahn wanted to (C)[rescue / abandon] Nigerians from hunger.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 내전으로 나라가 파괴되었고, 50만 명 이상이 굶주리고 있었다. 한 박사는 나이지리아인들을 구하고 싶었다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) destroyed: 내전으로 파괴됨. constructed(건설하다)는 반대. ✅ (B) starving: 굶주림. thriving(번성하다)는 반대. ✅ (C) rescue: 구하다. abandon(포기하다)은 반대.
det.tip: destroyed(파괴된) ↔ constructed(건설된). starving(굶주리는) ↔ thriving(번성하는). rescue(구하다) ↔ abandon(버리다).

questions.passage: When Dr. Hahn got there, he learned that the staple food in Nigeria was a plant called cassava. Unfortunately, cassava was (A)[defenseless / immune] against viral and bacterial diseases, so it did not yield much crop. Knowing this, he decided to develop stronger cassava varieties with higher yields. However, Dr. Hahn faced a problem: there was not much information (B)[available / restricted] about cassava. Cassava was rarely studied or developed because it was not a (C)[cash / staple] crop.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 카사바는 질병에 무방비 상태였고, 정보가 많이 이용 가능하지 않았다. 환금 작물이 아니어서 연구되지 않았다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) defenseless: 질병에 무방비. immune(면역인)은 반대. ✅ (B) available: 이용 가능한 정보가 많지 않음. restricted(제한된)도 부정 의미이나 원문과 다름. ✅ (C) cash: 환금 작물. staple(주식)은 이미 앞에서 카사바가 주식이라고 했으므로 모순.
det.tip: defenseless(무방비의) ↔ immune(면역의). cash crop = 환금 작물, staple food = 주식.

questions.passage: Another obstacle Dr. Hahn faced was distributing the new varieties. Local farmers would not listen to a foreigner. To (A)[overcome / ignore] this problem, Dr. Hahn visited markets, churches, and schools and gave out the new varieties to Nigerian people for free. He went from one house to the next to let farmers know the (B)[superiority / inferiority] of these new varieties. The farmers soon realized the superiority of the new varieties, and more and more farmers started to (C)[cultivate / eliminate] them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이 문제를 극복하기 위해 무료 배포. 새 품종의 우수성을 알림. 농부들이 재배하기 시작.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) overcome: 문제를 극복하다. ignore(무시하다)는 문맥 불일치. ✅ (B) superiority: 우수성. inferiority(열등함)는 반대. ✅ (C) cultivate: 재배하다. eliminate(제거하다)는 반대.
det.tip: overcome(극복하다) ↔ ignore(무시하다). superiority(우수성) ↔ inferiority(열등함). cultivate(재배하다) ↔ eliminate(제거하다).

questions.passage: Dr. Hahn is an agriculturist who specialized in plant breeding. Growing up right after the Korean war, he knew what it was like to be hungry, and he wanted to help people in need. In 1971, he was given two ①<u>opportunities</u>. On his way to Cambridge for a job interview, he first stopped in Nigeria. There, he saw the country had been ②<u>destroyed</u> by a civil war. More than 2 million people had died, and more than half a million people were starving. Dr. Hahn wanted to ③<u>rescue</u> Nigerians from hunger. So, he ④<u>discouraged</u> his family and moved to Nigeria.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 한 박사는 가족을 설득하여(persuaded) 나이지리아로 이주했다. discouraged(낙담시키다)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①opportunities(기회): 원문 그대로. ✅ ②destroyed(파괴된): 원문 그대로. ✅ ③rescue(구하다): 원문 그대로. ❌ ④discouraged(낙담시키다): 원문은 persuaded(설득하다). 가족을 설득한 맥락에서 '낙담시키다'는 반대.
det.tip: persuaded(설득하다) ↔ discouraged(낙담시키다). 가족과 함께 이주하려면 '설득'이 자연스러움.

questions.passage: While studying African cassava, Dr. Hahn found out that the Europeans who colonized Brazil had first brought cassava into Africa. He immediately flew to Brazil to study the original cassava. Then, Dr. Hahn traveled to every corner of Nigeria and ①<u>collected</u> different types of local cassava to see if they were good at fighting diseases, but they weren't. Fortunately, he found a plant that was similar to cassava but ②<u>resistant</u> to diseases. He started ③<u>crossing</u> this plant with the Brazilian cassava. After five years of hard work, Dr. Hahn finally ④<u>failed</u> in developing new varieties of cassava.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 5년간의 노력 끝에 한 박사는 새 품종 개발에 성공했다(succeeded). failed(실패하다)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①collected(수집하다): 원문 그대로. ✅ ②resistant(저항력 있는): 원문 그대로. ✅ ③crossing(교배하다): 원문 그대로. ❌ ④failed(실패하다): 원문은 succeeded(성공하다). 성공 서사에서 '실패'는 반대.
det.tip: succeeded(성공하다) ↔ failed(실패하다). 'finally succeeded' = 마침내 성공했다.

questions.passage: Another obstacle Dr. Hahn faced was distributing the new varieties. Local farmers would not listen to a foreigner. To overcome this problem, Dr. Hahn visited markets, churches, and schools and gave out the new varieties for free. His colleagues were ①<u>concerned</u> that the farmers might be angry. However, Dr. Hahn ②<u>insisted</u> that the farmers would think that it was a gift from God. The farmers soon realized the superiority of the new varieties, and more and more farmers started to cultivate them. Thanks to the new cassava, ③<u>fewer</u> people were starving. Eventually, Nigeria became the country that produced the ④<u>least</u> amount of cassava in the world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나이지리아는 세계에서 카사바를 가장 많이(greatest) 생산하는 나라가 되었다. least(가장 적은)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①concerned(걱정한): 원문 그대로. ✅ ②insisted(주장한): 원문 그대로. ✅ ③fewer(더 적은): 원문 그대로 — 굶주리는 사람이 줄었다. ❌ ④least(가장 적은): 원문은 greatest(가장 많은). 성공 결과 맥락에서 반대.
det.tip: greatest(가장 많은) ↔ least(가장 적은). 성공 스토리의 결론 = 가장 많이 생산.

questions.passage: Dr. Hahn is an agriculturist who specialized in plant breeding. Growing up right after the Korean war, he knew what it was like to be hungry, and he wanted to help people in need. In 1971, he was given two opportunities: work for Cambridge University or for the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture in Nigeria. On his way to Cambridge for a job interview, he first stopped in Nigeria. There, he saw the country had been destroyed by a civil war. More than 2 million people had died, and more than half a million people were __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 200만 명 이상이 죽었고, 50만 명 이상이 굶주리고 있었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②starving: 전쟁 후 죽음+기아 맥락. ❌ ①prospering(번영하는): 전쟁 파괴와 반대. ❌ ③celebrating(축하하는): 맥락 부적절. ❌ ④migrating(이주하는): 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: destroyed + died → starving. 전쟁 피해의 연쇄: 파괴 → 사망 → 기아.

questions.passage: When Dr. Hahn got there, he learned that the staple food in Nigeria was a plant called cassava. Unfortunately, cassava was defenseless against viral and bacterial diseases, so it did not yield much crop. Knowing this, he decided to develop stronger cassava varieties with higher yields. However, Dr. Hahn faced a problem: there was not much information available about cassava. Cassava was rarely studied or developed because it was not a __________ crop.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 카사바는 환금 작물이 아니었기 때문에 거의 연구되지 않았다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①cash: 환금 작물이 아니어서 연구 부족. ❌ ②organic(유기농): 맥락 무관. ❌ ③seasonal(계절): 연구 부족 이유 안 됨. ❌ ④tropical(열대): 이미 열대 농업 연구소인데 연구 안 된 이유 불일치.
det.tip: cash crop = 환금 작물 (시장에서 팔아 돈이 되는 작물). ↔ staple food = 주식.

questions.passage: Another obstacle Dr. Hahn faced was distributing the new varieties. Local farmers would not listen to a foreigner. To overcome this problem, Dr. Hahn visited markets, churches, and schools and gave out the new varieties to Nigerian people for free. Sometimes he planted them in the middle of the cassava field without telling the farmers. His colleagues were concerned that the farmers might be angry to find different cassava in their fields. However, Dr. Hahn __________ that the farmers would think that it was a gift from God. He was right.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 동료들은 걱정했지만, 한 박사는 농부들이 신의 선물이라 생각할 것이라고 주장했다. 그리고 그가 옳았다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③insisted: However 뒤에서 동료의 걱정에 반대되는 확신. 'He was right' 확인. ❌ ①doubted(의심하다): 확신과 반대. ❌ ②denied(부인하다): 맥락 불일치. ❌ ④regretted(후회하다): 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: However + insisted: 반대 견해에도 불구하고 확신을 갖고 주장. He was right = 결과적 확인.

questions.passage: There is a Korean man who became the chief of a Nigerian tribe for making huge <u>contributions</u> to Nigeria's agriculture and economy. Here is his story.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'contributions'와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 나이지리아의 농업과 경제에 큰 기여를 한 한국인.
det.analysis: ✅ ④donations: 기여, 공헌의 의미. contributions = 기여/공헌. ❌ ①restrictions(제한): 무관. ❌ ②objections(이의): 무관. ❌ ③competitions(경쟁): 무관.
det.tip: contribution(기여) ≈ donation(기증/기여). make contributions to = ~에 기여하다.

questions.passage: Dr. Hahn wanted to rescue Nigerians from hunger. So, he <u>persuaded</u> his family and moved to Nigeria.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'persuaded'와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 한 박사는 가족을 설득하여 나이지리아로 이주했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②convinced: 설득하다. persuaded와 동의어. ❌ ①threatened(위협하다): 반대 느낌. ❌ ③deceived(속이다): 부정적. ❌ ④abandoned(버리다): 무관.
det.tip: persuade = convince: 설득하다. persuade A to V = A를 설득하여 ~하게 하다.

questions.passage: Fortunately, he found a plant that was similar to cassava but <u>resistant</u> to diseases. He started crossing this plant with the Brazilian cassava.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'resistant'와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 질병에 저항력이 있는 식물을 발견했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①immune: 면역의, 저항력 있는. resistant와 유사. ❌ ②vulnerable(취약한): 반의어. ❌ ③sensitive(민감한): 반의어 느낌. ❌ ④exposed(노출된): 반의어 느낌.
det.tip: resistant(저항력 있는) ≈ immune(면역의). ↔ vulnerable(취약한).

questions.passage: Another obstacle Dr. Hahn faced was distributing the new varieties. Local farmers would not listen to a foreigner. He went from one house to the next to let farmers know the <u>superiority</u> of these new varieties.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'superiority'와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 새 품종의 우수성을 농부들에게 알렸다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③inferiority: 열등함. superiority의 정확한 반의어. ❌ ①excellence(탁월함): 유의어. ❌ ②dominance(지배): 유사 범주. ❌ ④authority(권위): 무관.
det.tip: superiority(우수성) ↔ inferiority(열등함). superior ↔ inferior.

questions.passage: Although he left Nigeria in 1994, he is still remembered as one of the greatest scientists who fought against starvation in Africa. Dr. Hahn once said, "If you have faith that what you do will benefit humanity, I believe that you must <u>sacrifice</u> yourself."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'sacrifice'와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 인류에 도움이 된다면 자신을 희생해야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②preserve: 보존하다. sacrifice(희생하다)의 반의어. 자신을 바치는 것 ↔ 자신을 보존. ❌ ①devote(헌신하다): 유사어. ❌ ③surrender(항복하다): 포기의 의미지만 반의어 아님. ❌ ④dedicate(바치다): 유사어.
det.tip: sacrifice(희생하다) ↔ preserve(보존하다). 자기를 바치다 ↔ 자기를 지키다.

questions.passage:
(A) Unfortunately, cassava was defenseless against viral and bacterial diseases, so it did not <u>yield</u> much crop.

(B) After five years of hard work, Dr. Hahn finally succeeded in developing new varieties of cassava. They <u>yield</u>ed much more than the local ones.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'yield'가 (A), (B)에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 수확물을 많이 산출하지 못했다. (B) 지역 품종보다 훨씬 많이 산출했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 두 문맥 모두 작물 생산의 의미. yield = 산출하다/생산하다. ❌ ①③: '항복하다'는 전쟁 맥락. ❌ ④: '양보하다'는 교통/논쟁 맥락.
det.tip: yield: ①산출하다(작물/결과) ②양보하다(교통) ③항복하다(전쟁). 여기서는 농업 맥락이므로 산출.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어를 고르시오.

"the main food that is eaten by people in a particular country or area"

det.korean: 특정 국가나 지역에서 주로 먹는 음식 = 주식(staple).
det.analysis: ✅ ③staple: 주식. 원문 'the staple food in Nigeria'. ❌ ①crop(작물): 주식이 아닌 작물 전반. ❌ ②variety(품종): 종류. ❌ ④seed(씨앗): 무관.
det.tip: staple food = 주식. staple: 주요한, 기본적인 → 주식.

questions.passage: There is a Korean man who became the chief of a Nigerian tribe. Dr. Hahn is an __________ (agriculture) who specialized in plant breeding. Growing up right after the Korean war, he knew what it was like to be hungry.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 한 박사는 식물 품종 개량을 전문으로 하는 농학자이다.
det.analysis: ✅ an + __________ → 관사 뒤 명사. agriculture(농업) → agriculturist(농학자).
det.tip: agriculture(농업, 명사) → agriculturist(농학자, 사람). -ist 접미사 = ~하는 사람.

questions.passage: When Dr. Hahn got there, he learned that the staple food in Nigeria was a plant called cassava. Unfortunately, cassava was __________ (defense) against viral and bacterial diseases, so it did not yield much crop. Knowing this, he decided to develop stronger varieties.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 카사바는 질병에 무방비 상태였다.
det.analysis: ✅ was + __________ → be동사 뒤 형용사. defense(방어) → defenseless(무방비의).
det.tip: defense(방어, 명사) → defenseless(방어할 수 없는, 형용사). -less 접미사 = ~없는.

questions.passage: While studying African cassava, Dr. Hahn found out that the Europeans who colonized Brazil had first brought cassava into Africa. He immediately flew to Brazil to study the original cassava. There, he learned about it and went back to Nigeria with Brazilian cassava seeds. Then, Dr. Hahn traveled to every corner of Nigeria and collected different types of local cassava to see if they were __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: easy to grow in all climates

det.korean: 지역 카사바가 질병 퇴치에 좋은지 확인하려고 수집했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④good at fighting diseases: 원문 그대로. 질병 저항력 확인 목적. ❌ ①: 수출 목적 아님. ❌ ②: 환금 작물 여부가 아님. ❌ ③: 기후 적응이 아님.
det.tip: 핵심 목적: 질병에 강한 카사바 개발 → 지역 품종의 질병 저항력 확인.

questions.passage: In addition to cassava, Dr. Hahn developed other major foods, including yam, sweet potato, and banana. Soon, other African countries asked for his help. Dr. Hahn traveled to these countries to teach local farmers and scholars how to grow these new varieties. He spent 23 years developing and distributing the new cassava varieties to the whole continent. Although he left Nigeria in 1994, he is still remembered as one of the greatest scientists who __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: discovered new species of tropical plants

det.korean: 아프리카의 기아와 싸운 가장 위대한 과학자 중 한 명으로 기억된다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③fought against starvation in Africa: 원문 그대로. 글 전체 주제. ❌ ①: 무역 협정 아님. ❌ ②: 새 종 발견이 아닌 품종 개량. ❌ ④: 대학 설립 아님.
det.tip: 글 전체의 핵심: 한 박사 = 아프리카 기아 퇴치에 헌신한 과학자.
